title: Benelux commercial launch field guide
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is a lightweight, field-ready briefing for the Benelux commercial launch (Belgium, Netherlands, Luxembourg). Primary audience: AE and Solutions Engineers, channel partners (system integrators), localized marketing managers. Secondary audience: product and sales ops for KPI tracking and channel enablement.

Top-level positioning (one-liner + 3 value pillars):
- One-liner: Redwood Inference brings predictable low-latency LLM serving with enterprise controls and cost-efficiency — now supported from Benelux regions and local partner capacity.
- Pillars:
  1) Predictable performance and SLAs: Dedicated capacity options and regional endpoints reduce latency for EU customers and simplify compliance.
  2) Cost controls for predictable P&L: Intelligent batching, quantization guidance, and per-route cost breakdowns make inference economical for production apps.
  3) Data sovereignty + enterprise-ready integrations: VPC Private deployments, KMS integrations, audit logs — meets procurement requirements for regulated industries.

Key customer segments to prioritize in Benelux:
- Fintechs & neobanks (NL/BE): low-latency conversational automation with strict audit requirements.
- Large SaaS vendors with EU customers: embed generative features with predictable unit economics.
- Public sector and regulated healthcare providers (select opportunities in BE/LUX).
- Local cloud native startups looking for multi-region reliability without heavy ops.

Top competitor landscape (notes for quick rebuttals):
- Big cloud providers (AWS/GCP/Azure managed endpoints): Strength = deep infra + marketplace procurement. Weakness = per-request cost unpredictability and limited inference optimizations for LLMs. Rebuttal: Redwood offers predictable token unit economics and model-optimized serving (batching/kv-caching) plus easier rollouts.
- LLM API incumbents (full-stack rivals): Strength = brand and large model catalogs. Weakness = fewer enterprise deployment options and less deterministic latency at scale. Rebuttal: Emphasize Dedicated + Private modes and per-route SLOs.
- Self-hosted inference vendors: Strength = customization. Weakness = ops burden. Rebuttal: Redwood reduces ops via managed stacks for Dedicated and Private control plane options.

Sales positioning & pitch outline (30s, 2min, technical):
- 30s elevator: "If you need predictable LLM performance and predictable costs with enterprise controls — without building your own inference stack — Redwood is the simplest way to ship."
- 2min: problem -> impact -> solution -> proof: succinctly cover latency/regulatory pain, cost leakage, Redwood features (Dedicated pools, Private VPC, Optimize suggestions), and call out pilot references / perf numbers.
- Technical (for SEs): discuss autoscaling policies, KV cache prefixing, quantization profiles, and how we fallback to compatible variants when capacity constrained. Have sequence length and token cost examples ready.

Common objections & suggested responses:
- "We can just use cloud managed endpoints": Acknowledge provider choice then compare predictable unit economics and batching optimizations that reduce long-term spend; offer a cost-savings analysis.
- "We need on-prem only": Confirm compliance needs; propose Redwood Private with on-prem package + HSM/KMS integrations and reference engagement checklist.
- "Vendor lock-in concerns": Explain model-agnostic runtime, exportable configs, version-pinable deployments; propose pilot with time-limited commit.

Launch assets available (quick checklist for field):
- Localized one-pager (EN/NL/FR) — draft attached to campaign folder.
- Sales playbook slide deck — contains ROI calculator and objection handling.
- Demo workspace: pre-configured demo showing chat, embeddings, and deduped billing.
- Technical FAQ for SEs — includes kernel/quantization profiling snippets.

Suggested announcement channels & timing:
- Week 0 (internal): All-hands + regional AMA with Product + SEs; notify Customer Success and AE with enablement session.
- Week 1 (soft public): Targeted email to existing Benelux customers and partners; LinkedIn company post timed with localized blog.
- Week 2 (broad GA): Press outreach to local tech press, regional webinars co-hosted with partners, partner referral incentives.

Sample customer-facing email subject lines (A/B test ideas):
- "Redwood Inference now in Benelux: faster LLM inference + regional control"
- "Reduce inference cost and latency for EU customers — Benelux regional endpoints"
- "Pilot Redwood Dedicated in your region — apply for a Benelux trial"

Internal enablement plan (for first 30 days):
- Day 0: Launch brief + SE enablement deck distributed.
- Day 2: Live SE workshop — hands-on demo with latency/cost playbook and troubleshooting runbook.
- Day 7: Sales office hours with product engineering for complex technical prospects.
- Day 14: Partner onboarding clinic for SIs and cloud partners.
- Ongoing: Weekly sync for feedback loop into product and messaging.

KPIs to track (initial 90 days):
- Pipeline created in Benelux (ARR)
- Number of pilot trials started and converted to paid Dedicated seats
- Average per-token cost for pilots vs baseline
- Latency percentile improvements for regional endpoints
- Partner-sourced deals count

Localization notes (NL/FR):
- Messaging nuance: in NL emphasize speed and scale for product teams; in FR/BE emphasize compliance and procurement readiness. Use local case studies and translate assets. Avoid generic EU phrasing — call out Benelux region name.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Pricing floor for Benelux Dedicated pilots (need finance sign-off) — linked JIRA RDW-4521.
- Partner referral rate and contract template (legal input required).
- Commitment for localized support hours for first 3 months.

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Finalize NL/FR one-pager: Maya (due 2026-02-19).
- Draft partner engagement email and list of target SIs: Lukas (due 2026-02-16).
- Cost-savings pilot template + sample TCO: Ethan (due 2026-02-18).
- Schedule internal SE workshop and record for on-demand: Sofia (owner) (scheduled 2026-02-20).

Appendix: Tactical talking points for SEs (copy/paste friendly)
- "We see customers typically reduce per-token costs by 20–40% after applying Redwood Optimize recommendations — batching, caching, and model suggestions."
- "Dedicated pools give you predictable throughput and SLOs, especially useful for chat endpoints with strict latency targets."
- "If compliance requires local data residency, we offer Private deploys with a customer-managed control plane and KMS/HSM integrations."

Notes to self / draft tone suggestions:
- Keep external messaging concise and benefit-focused. Use technical details in collateral for SEs and developer audiences. Avoid overclaiming — reference regression monitoring and rollback safeguards.

End of doc.
